general: Keep your threat under 32 and Ungoliant's Spawn will not engage you; keep it under 40 and neither will the Hummerhorns. There is not much point going lower than that, as most of the other enemies here engage cheaply anyway.

Don't take undefended attacks. Several shadow cards in this deck have a second effect that only fires when nobody defended, and they hit hard: the Spawn raises your threat by 8 instead of 4, and the Hummerhorns deal 2 damage to every character you control instead of 1.

Don't put Ungoliant's Spawn in the victory display. One of the two stage 3 cards is won by finding and defeating it, and it only searches the encounter deck and the discard pile, so a Spawn sitting in the victory display leaves you nothing to find.

If you are playing the Core Set's four pre-made decks, don't expect the Tactics one to get through this. It has almost no willpower, so it only wins when the encounter deck happens to deal it enemies to kill. Merge it with another sphere first.

1: Have a defender ready in the first round or two. Setup drops a Forest Spider straight into the staging area, it engages at 25, and its Forced effect gives it +1 attack for the round as soon as it reaches you, so it hits for 3.
2: Stage 2 only needs 2 quest points, so a normal quest phase will take you straight past it. Clear what you can out of the staging area first, as beating this stage sends you to one of the two stage 3 cards at random and you don't get to pick.
3: If Ungoliant's Spawn turns up early, don't kill it outright. Get its 9 hit points as low as you can and advance with it still in play: "Don't Leave the Path!" is won by defeating it, and Beorn's Path can't be beaten while it is on the table, so either way you want it one hit from dead.
